Common questions

Frequently asked questions

If you have a question not answered here, send us a note at courses@evalcourses.org and we'll respond within one business day.

About the course

  • No prior experience is required. The course is designed for people who are already in roles where grant writing is expected of them — whether or not they've had formal training. If you've been writing grants by instinct, template, or trial and error, this course will give you the reasoning behind what actually works.

    That said, the course will be most useful if you have some context for the nonprofit sector — if you understand what a program is, what a budget is, and what a funder is, you're ready to start.

  • Every session is recorded and available within 24 hours. You can watch at your own pace and still complete all the worksheets. The live sessions are valuable — you get Q&A time and the chance to work through real examples with peers — but they're not required to get full benefit from the course.

    If you know you'll miss most of the live sessions, this course will still serve you well as a self-paced program. If your schedule is completely unpredictable for the next two months, we'd suggest waiting for a future cohort when you have more flexibility.

  • Plan for roughly two to three hours per week. The live session is 90 minutes. The weekly worksheet takes about 45 minutes to an hour, depending on how much time you want to spend applying it to a real grant you're working on. There's no reading assigned between sessions.

  • The course does not include individual proposal review from Elena — that's a consulting service priced separately. What you will get is the chance to bring questions about your own grants to the live Q&A portion of each session. Elena regularly walks through examples volunteers share during class, and many students find this gives them the specific feedback they need.

    If you need one-on-one proposal review, information about Elena's consulting services is available on request.

  • We cap each cohort at 35 students to ensure Elena has time for real Q&A and to keep the group discussions productive. The September cohort has historically filled before the enrollment deadline, so we'd encourage you to sign up as soon as you've decided — not to create urgency artificially, but because it does fill.

  • No. Practical Grant Writing focuses entirely on private foundation and corporate grants. Federal grants (HRSA, SAMHSA, HUD, etc.) involve a different language of compliance, forms, and formatting requirements that would require a dedicated course to cover responsibly. If federal grants are your primary need, this course is not the right fit.

Logistics & Access

  • A computer, a reliable internet connection, and a web browser. Live sessions are hosted on Zoom (free to join). Course materials and recordings are accessible through a simple web portal — no additional software required. Worksheets are provided as downloadable PDFs and editable Google Docs.

  • Yes. Organizations enrolling two or more staff members in the same cohort receive a discounted group rate. Email us at courses@evalcourses.org to arrange a group enrollment before purchasing individual seats.

  • On the enrollment form, check the box indicating you'd like to be considered for a scholarship seat and provide a brief description of your organization — its mission, the community you serve, and your approximate annual budget. We review applications on a rolling basis and typically respond within five business days.

    Each cohort has three scholarship seats available for grassroots organizations with annual budgets under $500,000. We prioritize BIPOC-led organizations, rural nonprofits, and organizations in geographies with limited local foundation support.

  • Full refunds are available until September 3 — one week before the course begins. After that date, refunds are not available, but your enrollment can be transferred to the next cohort at no additional charge. If you have an unexpected conflict arise after enrollment, just reach out and we'll work with you.

  • Yes. Students who complete the six-week course and submit all worksheets receive a certificate of completion from Eval Course Education. The certificate includes Elena's name, the course title, and the cohort dates — suitable for professional development portfolios and LinkedIn.

  • You'll retain permanent access to all session recordings, worksheets, and template materials — with no expiration date. The course is designed to be a resource you return to regularly, not something you use once and set aside. Many alumni revisit the budget and outcomes sessions before major proposal deadlines.

    We also host a periodic alumni Q&A with Elena (quarterly, announced by email) where past students can bring current proposals for discussion. Attendance is free for all alumni.
